\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಇಂಧನ} (indhana)}{ಇಂಧನ (indhana)}]{\kn{ಇಂಧನ} (indhana) — fuel}

\label{lesson:KA-C448-indhana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to stall, then the Kannada for to ply.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಇಂಧನ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಇಂಧನ}} — \emph{indhana} — \textquotedblleft{}fuel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ವಿಮಾನಕ್ಕೆ} \kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ಇಂಧನ} \kn{ಬೇಕು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimānakke tumbā indhana bēku.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
An aeroplane needs a lot of fuel.
\end{quote}

Petrol, diesel, gas and firewood are all \kn{ಇಂಧನ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಇಂಧನ}} (\emph{indhana}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{indhana}, \textquotedblleft{}lighting, kindling, fuel\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1584), from \emph{indh}, \textquotedblleft{}to kindle\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indhana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indhana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānakke tumbā indhana bēku.} — An aeroplane needs a lot of fuel.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to stall, then the Kannada for to ply, then say \emph{indhana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಇಂಧನ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fuel\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಡೀಸೆಲ್} (ḍīsel)}{ಡೀಸೆಲ್ (ḍīsel)}]{\kn{ಡೀಸೆಲ್} (ḍīsel) — diesel}

\label{lesson:KA-C448-disel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to ply, then the Kannada for fuel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಡೀಸೆಲ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಡೀಸೆಲ್}} — \emph{ḍīsel} — \textquotedblleft{}diesel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಈ} \kn{ಬಸ್} \kn{ಡೀಸೆಲ್ನಿಂದ} \kn{ಓಡುತ್ತದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ī bas ḍīselninda ōḍuttade.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This bus runs on diesel.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಪೆಟ್ರೋಲ್} and \kn{ಡೀಸೆಲ್} are sold side by side.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಡೀಸೆಲ್}} (\emph{ḍīsel}) is a loan from English \emph{diesel}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍīsel}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ī bas ḍīselninda ōḍuttade.} — This bus runs on diesel.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to ply, then the Kannada for fuel, then say \emph{ḍīsel} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಬಂಕ್} (baṅk)}{ಬಂಕ್ (baṅk)}]{\kn{ಬಂಕ್} (baṅk) — a fuel station; a petrol pump}

\label{lesson:KA-C448-bank}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for fuel, then the Kannada for diesel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬಂಕ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಂಕ್}} — \emph{baṅk} — \textquotedblleft{}a fuel station; a petrol pump\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಹೆದ್ದಾರಿಯ} \kn{ಪಕ್ಕದ} \kn{ಬಂಕ್ನಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಪೆಟ್ರೋಲ್} \kn{ತುಂಬಿಸಿದೆವು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{heddāriya pakkada baṅknalli peṭrōl tumbisidevu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We filled up with petrol at the fuel station beside the highway.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಪೆಟ್ರೋಲ್} \kn{ಬಂಕ್} is the full name.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಂಕ್}} (\emph{baṅk}) is a loan from English \emph{bunk}, in Indian use, in the phrase \emph{petrol bunk}, \textquotedblleft{}a fuel station\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṅk}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṅk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{heddāriya pakkada baṅknalli peṭrōl tumbisidevu.} — We filled up with petrol at the fuel station beside the highway.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for fuel, then the Kannada for diesel, then say \emph{baṅk} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ} (byāṭari)}{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ (byāṭari)}]{\kn{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ} (byāṭari) — a battery}

\label{lesson:KA-C448-byatari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for diesel, then the Kannada for a fuel station.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ}} — \emph{byāṭari} — \textquotedblleft{}a battery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ಫೋನಿನ} \kn{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ} \kn{ಮುಗಿಯಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nanna phōnina byāṭari mugiyitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My phone battery ran out.
\end{quote}

In speech \kn{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ} also names an electric torch.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿ}} (\emph{byāṭari}) is a loan from English \emph{battery}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{byāṭari}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for diesel, then the Kannada for a fuel station, then say \emph{byāṭari} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸವಾರಿ} \kn{ಮಾಡು} (savāri māḍu)}{ಸವಾರಿ ಮಾಡು (savāri māḍu)}]{\kn{ಸವಾರಿ} \kn{ಮಾಡು} (savāri māḍu) — to ride}

\label{lesson:KA-C448-savari-madu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a fuel station, then the Kannada for a battery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸವಾರಿ} \kn{ಮಾಡು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸವಾರಿ} \kn{ಮಾಡು}} — \emph{savāri māḍu} — \textquotedblleft{}to ride\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಮಕ್ಕಳು} \kn{ಕಡಲತೀರದಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಕುದುರೆ} \kn{ಸವಾರಿ} \kn{ಮಾಡಿದರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{makkaḷu kaḍalatīradalli kudure savāri māḍidaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children rode horses on the beach.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಸವಾರಿ} \kn{ಮಾಡಿದೆ}, \emph{savāri māḍide}.

\kn{ಕುದುರೆ} \kn{ಸವಾರಿ}, horse riding; \kn{ಸವಾರ}, a rider.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಸವಾರಿ} \kn{ಮಾಡು}} (\emph{savāri māḍu}) joins \emph{savāri}, \textquotedblleft{}a ride\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{savārī}, \textquotedblleft{}riding, a mount\textquotedblright{}, through Hindustani, and the native verb \kn{ಮಾಡು}, to do.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{savāri māḍu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{savāri māḍu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{makkaḷu kaḍalatīradalli kudure savāri māḍidaru.} — The children rode horses on the beach.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a fuel station, then the Kannada for a battery, then say \emph{savāri māḍu} again
\end{itemize}
